name: Navbar
description: Top navigation bar of the application: brand on the left, a list of NavbarItems in the center and actions on the right. On mobile, the sections open in a dropdown panel from a menu button.

dos: Spans the page width and sits at the start of the document, inside `header`. Only one main navigation bar per page.
Put only `NavbarItem` elements in the list. Mark `active` on the one for the current section.
Use `variant="subtle"` when the bar sits on an already tinted surface; `solid` (default) on the page background.
Use `showActions={false}` when the page needs no actions (e.g. a sign-up screen) so the bar does not show empty buttons.

donts.case: Navigation menu inside the page content, or a side menu
donts.useInstead: Tabs or a list of links inside the content
donts.why: The bar is the application's global navigation. Repeating it or using it for an internal section confuses the navigation order.

donts.case: Putting loose text links or buttons inside the bar, outside the navigation list or the actions
donts.useInstead: NavbarItem for sections; Button for actions
donts.why: This way each element has the bar's style, focus and state. A loose Link breaks the height and spacing.

donts.case: More than two actions in the bar
donts.useInstead: An actions menu (dropdown) inside the page
donts.why: Figma defines two actions (a secondary and a primary one). With more, the bar does not fit on mobile.

donts.case: A tab bar to switch views of the same content
donts.why: Navbar navigates between sections of the application; Tabs switches views within a page.

related.difference: Each element in the navigation list is a NavbarItem.
The bar's actions are Buttons (one secondary and one primary).
The menu button on mobile is a ghost IconButton.

props.name: variant
props.description: Bar background. solid = page background (page-background); subtle = neutral.2 surface. In Figma, the component set's default is solid.

props.name: open
props.description: Mobile only. If true, opens the panel with the NavbarItem list and the actions, and changes the menu button icon to "x". On desktop nothing changes: in Figma, open=true and open=false look the same.

props.name: showActions
props.description: If true, shows the actions group (two Buttons). If false, the group is not rendered on desktop or in the mobile panel.

controlled.name: open
controlled.description: Mobile menu panel expanded. The menu button has aria-expanded="true" and its icon changes to "x".

root.description: Root element. Contains the bar and, on mobile with open=true, the menu panel.

bar.description: Row with the brand on the left and the navigation and actions groups on the right (on mobile, the menu button).

brand.description: Brand: logo and name. Minimum height of 40 px.

logo.description: 20 × 20 px logo. In Figma it is an empty frame: no image or icon is defined.

name.description: Brand name, fixed text "Mokkapp" in Figma. It is not a component property.

nav.description: List of application sections on desktop. Contains NavbarItems.

actions.description: Actions group: on desktop, at the right of the bar; on mobile, inside the panel. Visible only with showActions=true.

menuToggle.description: Menu button, mobile only. It is a ghost neutral IconButton of size 3 (40 × 40 px). Its icon is "menu" with open=false and "x" with open=true. Has aria-expanded and aria-controls.

menu.description: Mobile menu panel. Only with open=true. List of full-width NavbarItems and full-width actions below.

height.note: Bar height: 64 px = 12 px vertical padding + 40 px of the brand/menu button. On mobile with open=true, the height goes up to 320 px (64 bar + 256 panel).

width.note: In Figma, the root takes 1280 px on desktop and 375 px on mobile, with the width of its viewport.

autoLayout.gap: No gap on the root. The bar is HORIZONTAL, SPACE_BETWEEN, cross-centered, and its width is FILL.

events.name: onOpenChange
events.trigger: Pressing the menu button on mobile (open or close the panel). Not in Figma: needed to control `open`.

a11y.role: banner (implicit from header outside main); the list of sections is navigation (nav)
a11y.name: The header does not need a name. The nav, if there is more than one on the page, needs aria-label. The menu button needs aria-label (IconButton requires it).
keyboard: Tab — moves through brand, sections and actions in order
Enter / Space — on the menu button, opens or closes the panel
Escape — closes the mobile panel and returns focus to the menu button (proposal, not in Figma)
a11y.focusIndicator: Inherited by NavbarItem, Button and IconButton from their contracts. The bar adds no ring of its own.
a11y.minTarget: 40 × 40 px menu button; list items 32 px tall; the width depends on the text. All ≥ 24 × 24 px (WCAG 2.5.8).
a11y.contrastNote: neutral.12 brand text on the bar background (page-background or neutral.2). Not measured in Figma.
wcag: 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (the bar sits at the start of the document)

label.voice: Only the brand name ("Mokkapp") is fixed in Figma. The navigation texts belong to NavbarItem and the action labels belong to Button.

behavior.overflow: nowrap in the bar: texts do not wrap. With many sections on desktop, no truncation is defined in Figma.

responsive.desktop: List of NavbarItems in the bar, actions on the right, no menu button. Horizontal padding 32 px.
responsive.mobile: Brand on the left, menu button on the right (40 × 40 px). When opened, panel with full-width NavbarItems and actions. Horizontal padding 16 px.

i18n.rtl: The bar uses SPACE_BETWEEN: in RTL the brand moves to the right. The menu button also changes sides. Check that the order of the sections follows the language.
i18n.textExpansion: The brand name and each NavbarItem grow in width. On mobile, the panel must still fit; on desktop, the list may push the actions out of the bar.

cases: renders a header with a bar and a nav list of NavbarItems
variant=solid uses tokens.colors.page-background; variant=subtle uses colors.neutral.neutral.2
showActions=false renders the actions group neither on desktop nor in the mobile panel
open=true on mobile shows the panel and the "x" icon; on desktop the layout does not change
the menu button has aria-expanded matching open
the height is 64 px; with open=true on mobile, 320 px
the horizontal padding is spacing.6 on desktop and spacing.4 on mobile
Tab moves through brand, sections and actions in DOM order
Escape closes the mobile panel and returns focus to the menu button

needsReview: The component set has 8 variants: breakpoint (desktop, mobile) × variant (solid, subtle) × open (false, true). All were read. Same layers in all of them, except the menu panel (mobile open=true only) and the menu button (mobile only).

Property `breakpoint` (desktop/mobile): not a prop. Documented in behavior.responsive, because in code it is a media query, not a prop. Proposed decision: do not expose it as a prop. If the design needs to force mobile for documentation, decide it here. The breakpoint between desktop (1280 px) and mobile (375 px) is not defined in Figma.
Property `open` (false/true): exposed as the controlled prop `open`. On desktop it has no visual effect in Figma.
Property `showActions` (BOOLEAN, default true): controls the actions group on both desktop and the mobile panel. Exposed as the showActions prop.
Logo: empty 20 × 20 px frame in Figma (no image, fill or icon). What goes there still needs to be defined: image, icon or slot. Until then, the logo has no content in the contract.
Brand name "Mokkapp": fixed text in Figma, not a property. Pending decision: fixed text of the component, or add a text property (or `brand` slot) in Figma. No prop has been added in code.

List of sections and actions: in Figma they are fixed instances (4 NavbarItems and 2 Buttons), with no slot property or instance swap. The contract models them as slots with figmaProp null. minItems of the list (1) and mandatory (true) are proposed decisions.

NavbarItems appear twice in Figma: in the bar (desktop) and in the panel (mobile). Proposed decision: in code, a single list rearranged with CSS, to avoid duplicating nodes. If two lists are wanted, change anatomy.

Menu button icon: it is an instance swap that changes with open (menu → x). Solved in code with the open prop; there is no icon prop in the contract. The menu button is an IconButton (ghost, neutral, size 3, highContrast false) with its own contract. The button's aria-label is not in Figma: text still to be defined (e.g. "Open menu" / "Close menu").

The two action buttons are Buttons (variant soft and solid, color accent, size 2) with texts "Entrar" and "Empezar". The texts are instance overrides, not Navbar properties. They are left as the content of the actions slot.

Measurements with no variable in Figma: logo 20 × 20 px; root height 64 px and 320 px open (result of padding + brand height); mobile panel 256 px tall; bar padding 12 px vertical and gap between brand and name. Most of them match existing tokens (spacing.*, tokens.space.button-height-3), but only by value, not by variable. The panel sizes have no token.

Root stroke: neutral-alpha.6 with 0.15 opacity on the stroke itself. The color token is bound, but the 0.15 opacity has no token and the stroke position (inside/outside, bottom border) could not be read. The color and the 1 px width are documented; verify by hand.
Solid background: tokens.colors.page-background (bound in Figma). Subtle background: colors.neutral.neutral.2 (bound).
Brand text: text-style.4.bold (18 px, 26 px tall, -0.04 px letter spacing) bound to variables. Color neutral.12.

Product content written as a draft, it does not come from Figma: description, guidance, a11y (including Escape to close the panel, which is not in Figma), events (onOpenChange), testing, content and the dont's. Decisions I made: header as the root element, nav for the list, `subtle` as the surface variant, and showActions=false as a use case.
Brand element name: the contract models it as a div (brand) without a link. Figma does not say whether the logo + name lead to the home page: decide whether the brand is a link.
governance: null, same as Button. Component owners still need to be defined.
